whats_working: Question cards, section header, and step pills read as one calm green-on-cream system across all four platforms in light mode; the active step pill (dark green in light, mint fill in dark) and progress chip give a clear you-are-here signal (Norman:Mapping, UI:Consistency).

Footer nav (Back / Save & exit / Next) is persistent and sticky above the safe-area inset with bottomInset+12 padding, so the primary Next CTA stays in the thumb zone and clears the iPhone home indicator (Mobile:ThumbZone, iphone dark 12).

Option rows are built from a pressable XStack rather than a fixed-height Button specifically so long labels wrap and the row grows (SelectionButton comment, line 1287) — verified on 'Only a few times (less than once a month)' and 'I have not been here in the last 6 months' which wrap cleanly on phone.
Read-only Generated auditor ID and Audit date fields are visually distinct (uppercase micro-label, surface fill) so auditors don't mistake them for editable inputs (Norman:Signifiers, ipad dark 08).

findings.title: Dark mode: every unselected answer label is mint-green, so nothing looks selected (or everything does)
findings.evidence: packs/audit-placeId-step.md line 1312: unselected label color = palette.accent, and getSurveyPalette (line 1800) sets accent = designSystem.colors.primary, which is #7FBFA3 in dark. In iphone/dark/12-audit-domain-questions.png and ipad/dark/09 every unselected option ('Yes', 'No', 'I'm not sure', 'Spring'...'Winter', all weather rows) renders green on the input surface #1B1D19, while a SELECTED row would show primaryForeground on the same primary green fill. Unselected therefore reads as an active/link state and there is almost no perceptual difference between chosen and unchosen. Light mode is unaffected because primary #10231F is near-black.
findings.why: The whole point of a radio list is that selected vs unselected is instantly readable. Tinting every unselected label with the brand fill color removes that signifier and also breaks the DESIGN.md rule that fill tokens (primary/success) must not be used as text on soft backgrounds.
findings.fix: In SelectionButton, use designSystem.colors.foreground (#F3F1EC dark) for unselected labels and reserve palette.selected fill + primaryForeground for the selected row; keep the green tint only for the selected border/fill. Equivalently set palette.accent-for-labels to secondaryForeground/foreground rather than primary.

findings.title: Tablet audit wizard is a stretched phone column, not the spec's sidebar + capped form
findings.evidence: packs line 437: getResponsiveContentContainerStyle(layout, { bottomPadding, gap: 20 }) is called with NO maxWidth override, so it falls back to layout.contentMaxWidth (1040-1200 on tablet, responsive-layout-tokens.ts) instead of formMaxWidth 600. In ipad/light/08 and android-tablet/light/08 the survey card spans nearly the full ~1032-1280pt canvas with the radio floating far left and a large dead zone to the right of each option; the step list is still a horizontal-scroll pill row. core.md spec: 'Audit wizard on tablet = PERSISTENT left step sidebar + form at formMaxWidth'.
findings.why: Wide single-column survey rows with a lone left radio and long line-lengths are harder to scan than a 600pt reading column, and the horizontal-scroll step pills hide steps 6-8 off-screen on a canvas that has room for a full vertical sidebar. This is the tablet-only regression the design system explicitly warns against.
findings.fix: Pass maxWidth: layout.formMaxWidth to getResponsiveContentContainerStyle on tablet, and on isTablet render StepHeader's pill list as a persistent left rail (TwoPaneLayout) instead of a horizontal ScrollView so all 8 steps and the form-at-600 sit side by side.

findings.title: Whole wizard uses raw Text/Paragraph, so font-scale, dyslexic font, and tablet x1.3 do nothing
findings.evidence: packs line 25 imports Text, Paragraph directly from tamagui and every component (Card, QuestionCard, SelectionButton, ChoiceQuestion, ReadOnlyField) uses fixed fontSize literals (30, 22, 16, 11...) with no fontScale. Only YeeStackHeaderTitle applies designSystem.fontScale. core.md: 'Text must use ScaledText/ScaledParagraph; tablets x1.3.' Result: raising the accessibility text-size slider or enabling OpenDyslexic has no effect on any audit question, and the tablet base x1.3 is not applied — which is why option text looks small against the large tablet canvas in ipad/light/09.
findings.why: Auditors do fieldwork outdoors and this app ships an explicit readability/dyslexia mode; a survey with dozens of long questions is exactly where scalable, dyslexia-friendly text matters most, and it silently ignores those preferences.
findings.fix: Swap Text->ScaledText and Paragraph->ScaledParagraph (components/ui) throughout this file, or multiply every fontSize by designSystem.fontScale via useDesignSystem(); use the dyslexicFonts family from getDesignSystem so the readability toggle applies here too.

findings.title: Tablet: radio button and its label are separated by a wide gap, weakening the row as one target
findings.evidence: SelectionButton (packs line 1291) is an items='center' XStack with the radio at the far left and label immediately after, but because the row stretches to contentMaxWidth on tablet (see tablet-audit-not-adapted finding) the filled area is huge while the radio+label cluster hugs the left edge — see ipad/light/08 'I have never been here before' and android-tablet/dark/08, where ~60% of each pill is empty. The whole row is still tappable, but visually the control and its label look adrift in a large empty button.
findings.why: A large mostly-empty pill with a tiny left-aligned control reads as unfinished and makes the tap affordance ambiguous (is only the radio clickable?).
findings.fix: Once the form is capped at formMaxWidth (600) this largely resolves; additionally consider left-aligning content within a maxWidth reading column so the radio+label stay visually bound.

findings.title: Header progress reads '1/8' while the in-page chip says 'Step 1 of 9'
findings.affected: StepHeader chip vs stack-header progress indicator
findings.evidence: packs StepHeader renders 'Step {step} of 9' twice (lines 609 and 654), but the top-right progress element in every screenshot (e.g. iphone/light/12, ipad/light/08) shows '1/8'. The '1/8' indicator is not in this pack (it lives in the stack header/YeeStackHeaderTitle area), so the exact source can't be confirmed here, but the two totals visibly disagree on screen.
findings.why: Two different totals for the same wizard on the same screen make the auditor unsure how many steps remain, undermining the progress model.
findings.fix: Pick one denominator (the config exposes mobileYeeSteps; step 9 is Final comments) and use it for both the chip and the top progress bar, or relabel the top bar to match 'of 9'.

findings.title: Horizontal step pills clip later steps with no scroll affordance
findings.evidence: StepHeader renders the 8 step buttons in an XStack with flexWrap='wrap' (packs line 672). On phone the row is clipped at the right edge ('4 A...' cut off in iphone/light/11, android-phone/dark/11) with no chevron or fade hinting more steps exist to the right; on tablet the same clipping cuts 'Use & Usa...' (ipad/light/08). Because it's flexWrap not a ScrollView, it's ambiguous whether the hidden pills are reachable.
findings.why: Auditors jump between domains via these pills; clipped pills with no affordance hide navigation and force discovery by trial (does it scroll? does it wrap?).
findings.fix: Wrap the pill row in a horizontal ScrollView with a right-edge fade/gradient, or on tablet promote it to the persistent sidebar (see tablet finding) where all steps are visible without scrolling.
